claims.text: The starting Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a nanocrystalline BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder may contain surface oxides acquired during milling.
SPS at 900–1000 °C produces competition between bulk densification and precipitation of fine coherent secondary phases.
At 800 °C, diffusion is insufficient for barrier-phase nucleation, bulk densification, and high hardness.
At 950–1000 °C, enhanced Al, Ti, and Fe diffusion precipitates a nanoscale secondary-phase network at grain boundaries.
The secondary phases are likely Mg-Al-Ti intermetallics or Mg-Fe-Co oxides.
The secondary phases impede dislocation motion and thereby increase hardness.
The secondary phases impede grain growth and provide Hall–Petch and Orowan strengthening.
A continuous secondary-phase network blocks oxygen and metal-ion diffusion and improves oxidation and corrosion resistance.
High mixing entropy stabilizes the BCC matrix during secondary-phase precipitation.
Negative Al-Ti or Fe-Co mixing enthalpies drive local segregation and nucleation of secondary phases.
SPS at 900–1000 °C for 10–15 minutes, at 50–100 °C/min and 50 MPa under vacuum or inert gas, is the proposed processing intervention.
Above 1000 °C, magnesium volatility causes substantial Mg loss and composition deviation.
Mg loss above 1000 °C causes coarse brittle intermetallics or porosity and reduces density and mechanical integrity.
The rate-limiting oxidation mechanism changes from diffusion-controlled below 900 °C to surface-reaction-limited above 950 °C after barrier formation.
The optimized bulk alloy will exceed 98% of theoretical density.
The optimized bulk alloy will have Vickers hardness above 600 HV.
The corrosion current density in 3.5 wt% NaCl will be below 0.5 µA/cm².
The optimized microstructure will be a BCC matrix containing a uniform distribution of nanoscale secondary phases.
Oxidation weight gain at 800 °C for 50 hours will be below 5 mg/cm².

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts surface-reaction-limited behavior above 950 °C after barrier formation, whereas the mechanism says the barrier blocks oxygen and metal-ion diffusion, which would instead make transport through the barrier the limiting process.

Linear oxidation kinetics at 950 °C are predicted as evidence of a surface-reaction-limited regime, but the falsification rule treats linear kinetics at 950 °C as evidence that the proposed barrier mechanism has failed.
